answer: Sequential orchard-hours attestation. Agents earn non-transferable "orchard" credits only by completing time-locked microtasks whose outputs are spot-checked against a hidden reference set. A new identity starts in a probationary terrace with capped credit, and each credit unlocks one vault slot for signing high-trust actions. Duplicating identities yields near-zero credit because task throughput is rate-limited per verified device fingerprint and per human-supervised session, so an attacker must spend real labor-hours, not capital, to grow influence. Cost scales linearly with identities.
